title: 1960 AHSME Problem 19
statement: Consider equation I: \(x+y+z=46,\) where \(x,\) \(y,\) and \(z\) are positive integers, and equation II: \(x+y+z+w=46,\) where \(x,\) \(y,\) \(z,\) and \(w\) are positive integers. Then:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: \(\mathrm{I}\) can be solved in consecutive integers

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: \(\mathrm{I}\) can be solved in consecutive even integers

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
\(\mathrm{II}\) can be solved in consecutive
integers

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: \(\mathrm{II}\) can be solved in consecutive even integers

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: \(\mathrm{II}\) can be solved in consecutive odd integers

solutions.text:
The sum of three consecutive integers is divisible by \(3,\) so it cannot be \(46.\) Four consecutive integers beginning with \(n\) have sum \(4n+6.\) Setting \(4n+6=46\) gives \(n=10,\) and indeed \[ 10+11+12+13=46. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Write the sums of three and four consecutive integers
Check which required average is compatible with \(46\)
